verses.zh: 犹大支派按着宗族拈阄所得之地是在尽南边，到以东的交界，向南直到寻的旷野。
verses.en: The land allotted to the tribe of Judah by its clans reached to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin in the Negev far to the south.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The lot was to the tribe of the sons of Judah by their clans to the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin toward the south, southward.”

verses.zh: 他们的南界是从盐海的尽边，就是从朝南的海汊起，
verses.en: Their southern border started at the southern tip of the Salt Sea,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the tongue that faces to the south.”sn The Salt Sea is another name for the Dead Sea (also in v. 5).

verses.zh: 通到亚克拉滨坡的南边，接连到寻，上到加低斯・巴尼亚的南边，又过希斯仑，上到亚达珥，绕到甲加，
verses.en: extended[NOTE:1] south of the Scorpion Ascent,[NOTE:2] crossed to Zin, went up from the south to Kadesh Barnea, crossed to Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka.
notes: Heb “went out.”
Or “the Ascent of Akrabbim” (עַקְרַבִּים [ʿaqrabbim] means “scorpions” in Hebrew).

verses.zh: 接连到押们，通到埃及小河，直通到海为止。这就是他们的南界。
verses.en: It then crossed to Azmon, extended to the Stream of Egypt,[NOTE:1] and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was their[NOTE:2] southern border.
notes: Traditionally “the Brook of Egypt,” although a number of recent translations have “the Wadi of Egypt” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV).
The translation follows the LXX at this point. The MT reads, “This will be your southern border.”

verses.zh: 东界是从盐海南边到约旦河口。北界是从约旦河口的海汊起，
verses.en: The eastern border was the Salt Sea to the mouth[NOTE:1] of the Jordan River.[NOTE:2] The northern border started north of the Salt Sea at the mouth of the Jordan,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “end.”
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied for clarity.
Heb “the border on the northern side was from the tongue of the sea, from the end of the Jordan.”

verses.zh: 上到伯・曷拉，过伯・亚拉巴的北边，上到流便之子波罕的磐石；
verses.en: went up to Beth Hoglah, crossed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

verses.zh: 从亚割谷往北，上到底璧，直向河南亚都冥坡对面的吉甲；又接连到隐・示麦泉，直通到隐・罗结，
verses.en: It then went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turning northward to Gilgal (which is opposite the Pass[NOTE:1] of Adummim south of the valley), crossed to the waters of En Shemesh, and extended to En Rogel.
notes: Or “ascent.”

verses.zh: 上到欣嫩子谷，贴近耶布斯的南界（耶布斯就是耶路撒冷）；又上到欣嫩谷西边的山顶，就是在利乏音谷极北的边界；
verses.en: It then went up the Valley of Ben Hinnom to the slope of the Jebusites on the south (that is, Jerusalem),[NOTE:1] going up to the top of the hill opposite the Valley of Ben Hinnom to the west, which is at the end of the Valley of the Rephaites to the north.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 又从山顶延到尼弗多亚的水源，通到以弗仑山的城邑，又延到巴拉（巴拉就是基列・耶琳）；
verses.en: It then went from the top of the hill to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, extended to the cities of Mount Ephron, and went to Baalah (that is, Kiriath Jearim).

verses.zh: 又从巴拉往西绕到西珥山，接连到耶琳山的北边（耶琳就是基撒仑）；又下到伯・示麦过亭纳，
verses.en: It then turned from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, crossed to the slope of Mount Jearim on the north (that is Kesalon), descended to Beth Shemesh, and crossed to Timnah.

verses.zh: 通到以革伦北边，延到施基仑，接连到巴拉山；又通到雅比聂，直通到海为止。
verses.en: It then extended to the slope of Ekron to the north, went toward Shikkeron, crossed to Mount Baalah, extended to Jabneel, and ended at the sea.

verses.zh: 西界就是大海和靠近大海之地。这是犹大人按着宗族所得之地四围的交界。
verses.en: The western border was the Mediterranean Sea.[NOTE:1] These were the borders of the tribe of Judah and its clans.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.
Heb “this was the border of the sons of Judah round about, by their clans.”

verses.zh: 约书亚照耶和华所吩咐的，将犹大人中的一段地，就是基列・亚巴，分给耶孚尼的儿子迦勒。亚巴是亚衲族的始祖（基列・亚巴就是希伯仑）。
verses.en: Caleb son of Jephunneh was assigned Kiriath Arba (that is Hebron) within the tribe of Judah, according to the Lord’s instructions to Joshua. (Arba was the father of Anak.)[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion in the midst of the sons of Judah according to the mouth [i.e., command] of the Lord to Joshua, Kiriath Arba (the father of Anak), it is Hebron.”

verses.zh: 迦勒就从那里赶出亚衲族的三个族长，就是示筛、亚希幔、挞买；
verses.en: Caleb drove out[NOTE:1] from there three Anakites—Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, descendants of Anak.
notes: Or “dispossessed.”

verses.zh: 又从那里上去，攻击底璧的居民。（这底璧从前名叫基列・西弗。）
verses.en: From there he attacked the people of Debir.[NOTE:1] (Debir used to be called Kiriath Sepher.)
notes: Heb “he went up against the inhabitants of Debir.”

verses.zh: 迦勒说：「谁能攻打基列・西弗将城夺取，我就把我女儿押撒给他为妻。」
verses.en: Caleb said, “To the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife.”

verses.zh: 迦勒兄弟基纳斯的儿子俄陀聂夺取了那城，迦勒就把女儿押撒给他为妻。
verses.en: When Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother,[NOTE:1] captured it, Caleb[NOTE:2] gave Achsah his daughter to him as a wife.
notes: “Caleb’s brother” may refer either to Othniel or to Kenaz. If Kenaz was the brother of Caleb, Othniel is Caleb’s nephew.
Heb “he”; the referent (Caleb) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 押撒过门的时候，劝丈夫向她父亲求一块田，押撒一下驴，迦勒问她说：「你要甚么？」
verses.en: One time Achsah[NOTE:1] came and charmed her father[NOTE:2] so that she could ask him for some land. When she got down from her donkey, Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”
notes: Heb “she”; the referent (Achsah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “him.” The referent of the pronoun could be Othniel, in which case the translation would be “she incited him [Othniel] to ask her father for a field.” This is problematic, however, for Achsah, not Othniel, makes the request in v. 19. The LXX has “he [Othniel] urged her to ask her father for a field.” This appears to be an attempt to reconcile the apparent inconsistency and probably does not reflect the original text. If Caleb is understood as the referent of the pronoun, the problem disappears. For a fuller discussion of the issue, see P. G. Mosca, “Who Seduced Whom? A Note on Joshua 15:18//Judges 1:14, ” CBQ 46 (1984): 18-22. This incident is also recorded in Judg 1:14.

verses.zh: 她说：「求你赐福给我，你既将我安置在南地，求你也给我水泉。」她父亲就把上泉下泉赐给她。
verses.en: She answered, “Please give me a special present.[NOTE:1] Since you have given me land in the Negev, now give me springs of water.” So he gave her both the upper and lower springs.
notes: Elsewhere this Hebrew word (בְּרָכָה, berakhah) is often translated “blessing,” but here it refers to a gift (as in Gen 33:11; 1 Sam 25:27; 30:26; 2 Kgs 5:15).

verses.zh: 以下是犹大支派按着宗族所得的产业。
verses.en: This is the land assigned to the tribe of Judah by its clans:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judah by their clans.”

verses.zh: 犹大支派尽南边的城邑，与以东交界相近的，就是甲薛、以得、雅姑珥、
verses.en: These cities were located at the southern extremity of Judah’s tribal land near the border of Edom:[NOTE:1] Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
notes: Heb “and the cities were at the end of the tribe of the sons of Judah, at the border of Edom, to the south.”

verses.zh: 基拿、底摩拿、亚大达、
verses.en: Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,

verses.zh: 基低斯、夏琐、以提楠、
verses.en: Kedesh, Hazor,[NOTE:1] Ithnan,
notes: For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.

verses.zh: 西弗、提链、比亚绿、
verses.en: Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,

verses.zh: 夏琐・哈大他、加略・希斯仑（加略・希斯仑就是夏琐）、
verses.en: Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor),

verses.zh: 亚曼、示玛、摩拉大、
verses.en: Amam, Shema, Moladah,

verses.zh: 哈萨・迦大、黑实门、伯・帕列、
verses.en: Hazar Gaddah, Heshbon, Beth Pelet,

verses.zh: 哈萨・书亚、别是巴、比斯约他、
verses.en: Hazar Shual, Beer Sheba, Biziothiah,

verses.zh: 巴拉、以因、以森、
verses.en: Baalah, Iim, Ezem,

verses.zh: 伊勒多腊、基失、何珥玛、
verses.en: Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,

verses.zh: 洗革拉、麦玛拿、三撒拿、
verses.en: Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,

verses.zh: 利巴勿、实忻、亚因、临门，共二十九座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon—a total of 29 cities and their towns.[NOTE:1]
notes: The total number of names in the list is thirty-six, not twenty-nine. Perhaps (1) some of the names are alternatives (though the text appears to delineate clearly such alternative names here and elsewhere, see vv. 8, 9, 10, 13, 25b) or (2), more likely, later scribes added to a list originally numbering twenty-nine and failed to harmonize the concluding summary statement with the expanded list.

verses.zh: 在高原有以实陶、琐拉、亚实拿、
verses.en: These cities were[NOTE:1] in the foothills:[NOTE:2] Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
notes: The words “these cities were” have been supplied for English stylistic reasons.
The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

verses.zh: 撒挪亚、隐・干宁、他普亚、以楠、
verses.en: Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,

verses.zh: 耶末、亚杜兰、梭哥、亚西加、
verses.en: Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,

verses.zh: 沙拉音、亚底他音、基底拉、基底罗他音，共十四座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Shaaraim, Adithaim, and Gederah (or Gederothaim)—a total of 14 cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有洗楠、哈大沙、麦大・迦得、
verses.en: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,

verses.zh: 底连、米斯巴、约帖、
verses.en: Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,

verses.zh: 拉吉、波斯加、伊矶伦、
verses.en: Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,

verses.zh: 迦本、拉幔、基提利、
verses.en: Cabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish,

verses.zh: 基低罗、伯・大衮、拿玛、玛基大，共十六座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—a total of 16 cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有立拿、以帖、亚珊、
verses.en: Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

verses.zh: 益弗他、亚实拿、尼悉、
verses.en: Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,

verses.zh: 基伊拉、亚革悉、玛利沙，共九座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—a total of nine cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有以革伦和属以革伦的镇市村庄；
verses.en: Ekron and its surrounding towns[NOTE:1] and settlements;
notes: Heb “daughters.”

verses.zh: 从以革伦直到海，一切靠近亚实突之地，并属其地的村庄。
verses.en: from Ekron westward, all those in the vicinity of Ashdod and their towns;

verses.zh: 亚实突和属亚实突的镇市村庄；迦萨和属迦萨的镇市村庄；直到埃及小河，并大海和靠近大海之地。
verses.en: Ashdod with its surrounding towns and settlements, and Gaza with its surrounding towns and settlements, as far as the Stream of Egypt[NOTE:1] and the border at the Mediterranean Sea.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on this place name in 15:4.
Heb “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.

verses.zh: 在山地有沙密、雅提珥、梭哥、
verses.en: These cities were[NOTE:1] in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
notes: The words “These cities were” have been supplied in the translation for English stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 大拿、基列・萨拿（基列・萨拿就是底璧）、
verses.en: Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir),

verses.zh: 亚拿伯、以实提莫、亚念、
verses.en: Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

verses.zh: 歌珊、何伦、基罗，共十一座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—a total of eleven cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有亚拉、度玛、以珊、
verses.en: Arab, Dumah,[NOTE:1] Eshan,
notes: Some Hebrew mss and some mss of the LXX read “Rumah” in place of “Dumah.”

verses.zh: 雅农、伯・他普亚、亚非加、
verses.en: Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,

verses.zh: 宏他、基列・亚巴（基列・亚巴就是希伯仑）、洗珥，共九座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior—a total of nine cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有玛云、迦密、西弗、淤他、
verses.en: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

verses.zh: 耶斯列、约甸、撒挪亚、
verses.en: Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,

verses.zh: 该隐、基比亚、亭纳，共十座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah—a total of 10 cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有哈忽、伯・夙、基突、
verses.en: Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,

verses.zh: 玛腊、伯・亚诺、伊勒提君，共六座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon—a total of six cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 又有基列・巴力（基列・巴力就是基列・耶琳）、拉巴，共两座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah—a total of two cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 在旷野有伯・亚拉巴、密丁、西迦迦、
verses.en: These cities were[NOTE:1] in the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
notes: The words “These cities were” have been supplied for English stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 匿珊、盐城、隐・基底，共六座城，还有属城的村庄。
verses.en: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi—a total of six cities and their towns.

verses.zh: 至于住耶路撒冷的耶布斯人，犹大人不能把他们赶出去，耶布斯人却在耶路撒冷与犹大人同住，直到今日。
verses.en: The men of Judah were unable to conquer the Jebusites living in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] The Jebusites live with the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this very day.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The statement to this very day reflects the perspective of the author, who must have written prior to David’s conquest of the Jebusites (see 2 Sam 5:6-7).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

Several items in Joshua point toward a contemporary date (in the day that Joshua lived).

- The ancient Canaanite names of cities are preserved.

- Baalah (Kiriath-jearim) ‒ Jos. 15:9

- Kiriath-sannah (Debir) ‒ Jos. 15:49

- Kiriath-arba (Hebron) ‒ Jos. 15:54

- Canaanites were still in control of

- Gezer ‒ Jos. 16:10

- Jebus ‒ Jos. 18:28

- Sidon, not Tyre, is listed as the main city of Phoenicia (cf. Jos. 13:4,6)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED TEXT): JOSHUA 15:1-12

1Now the lot for the tribe of the sons of Judah according to their families reached the border of Edom, southward to the wilderness of Zin at the extreme south. 2Their south border was from the lower end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that turns to the south. 3Then it proceeded southward to the ascent of Akrabbim and continued to Zin, then went up by the south of Kadesh-barnea and continued to Hezron, and went up to Addar and turned about to Karka. 4It continued to Azmon and proceeded to the brook of Egypt, and the border ended at the sea. This shall be your south border. 5The east border was the Salt Sea, as far as the mouth of the Jordan. And the border of the north side was from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan. 6Then the border went up to Beth-hoglah, and continued on the north of Beth-arabah, and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben. 7The border went up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and turned northward toward Gilgal which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south of the valley; and the border continued to the waters of En-shemesh and it ended at En-rogel. 8Then the border went up the valley of Ben-hinnom to the slope of the Jebusite on the south (that is, Jerusalem); and the border went up to the top of the mountain which is before the valley of Hinnom to the west, which is at the end of the valley of Rephaim toward the north. 9From the top of the mountain the border curved to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and proceeded to the cities of Mount Ephron, then the border curved to Baalah (that is, Kiriath-jearim). 10The border turned about from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and continued to the slope of Mount Jearim on the north (that is, Chesalon), and went down to Beth-shemesh and continued through Timnah. 11The border proceeded to the side of Ekron northward. Then the border curved to Shikkeron and continued to Mount Baalah and proceeded to Jabneel, and the border ended at the sea. 12The west border was at the Great Sea, even its coastline. This is the border around the sons of Judah according to their families.

15:1 "Now the lot for the tribe of the sons of Judah according to their families" The
tribe of Simeon was incorporated very early into the tribe of Judah and lost all of its identity (cf. Jos. 19:1-9).

▣ "Edom" This refers to the nation east of the Jordan which came from the
descendants of Esau. The basic meaning is "red" (BDB 10).

The term "south" (BDB 616) is Teman, which is the same term as the name
of one of Edom's major cities.

▣ "wilderness of Zin" This should not be confused with the Wilderness of Sin,
which is located in the southern part of the Sinai peninsula. This wilderness is in the northern
part of the Sinai peninsula in which Kadesh-barnea is located (cf. Num. 34:2-5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILDERNESSES OF THE EXODUS

15:3 "Akrabbim" This is the name for "scorpions" (BDB 785). The boundaries of the
Promised Land are given in Numbers 34 (cf. Num. 34:4). This pass was part of the unconquered
Amorite territory in Jdg. 1:36.

15:4 "the brook of Egypt" The term "brook" (BDB 636) is "wadi," which denotes a river
bed or channel which is dry part of the year. Today this one is called "Wadi El-arish."

Water (i.e., rivers, wadis, lakes, streams, oceans) were often used as boundaries.
This one is the most southern boundary of the Promised Land and Egypt (here the southern
boundary of Judah, cf. Num. 34:5).

Other natural barriers or topological distinctives, like valleys, mountain ranges,
plains, were also used as boundary markers.

15:6 "the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben" We know nothing about this young man or
why a memorial stone was raised for him. It is surely possible that this was a boundary marker and
not a memorial (cf. Jos. 18:17).

15:7 "Gilgal" This (BDB 166) does not refer to the first Israeli campsite (cf. Jos. 4:19). It is possible
that it should be translated "Geliloth" (BDB 165, cf. Jos. 18:17), because this location is also related to En-shemesh.

▣ "En-shemesh and. . . En-rogel" These were two springs (BDB 745) which
seem to be located on the road from Jericho to Jerusalem.

15:8 "the valley of Ben-hinnom . . . the valley of Hinnom" This is the place where the fertility
fire god, Molech, was worshiped. It was just outside the city of Jerusalem (Jebus, cf. Jos. 15:63) to
the south. This is the place which later the Jews turned into a garbage dump and which Jesus used
as His metaphor to describe Hell (Gehenna).

▣ "Rephaim" See notes at Jos. 11:21.

15:9 "Baalah" This seems to be the feminine form for the term baal, and it
may mean "mistress." It was the older name of Kiriath-jearim.

15:10 "Mount Seir" This means "rough," "hairy," or "shaggy" (BDB 973). There are
several different sites by this name. This does not refer to Mt. Seir in Edom, but a hill close to
Jerusalem.

▣ "Beth-shemesh" This means "house of the sun" (BDB 112, cf.
1 Sam. 6:9,12,13,15,19,20; 1 Kgs. 4:9; 2 Kgs. 14:13). Many believe that this refers to sun
worship. There are several cities by this name.

▣ "Timnah" This was a town which was later associated with the exploits of Samson.

15:11 "Ekron" This was one of the five main Philistine walled cities (cf. Jos. 15:45-47). Apparently
Judah never fully captured it or any of the main cities on the plain where chariot forces were used.
See NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 568-569.

15:12 "the Great Sea" This refers to the Mediterranean Ocean.

▣ "until this day" This use of the phrase shows that the scribe lived and wrote
before David's day. Because Moses grew up and was trained in Egypt, which explains why Jewish
scribes felt free to upgrade the literary works of Israel. From archaeology it is obvious that
Mesopotamian scribes never changed their national texts whereas Egyptian scribes felt free to
upgrade their national/religious texts. See notes at Jos. 7:26.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible
for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy
Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is the division of the land so important to the Jewish people?

- Did the Israelites fully occupy their tribal allocations?

- Who are the Nephilim and Anakim?

- What was the lot and how did it work?

- Describe the Canaanite fertility religion.
